narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Fresh model guidance brings refined timing for tonight's convective setup across the Nyanza Basin, with high atmospheric instability supporting thunderstorm potential through dusk and overnight. Rain chances remain elevated into Tuesday evening before a temporary break mid-week.

## Today's Forecast
With evening underway, attention shifts entirely to the overnight horizon as daytime heat and UV exposure are in the past. High atmospheric instability (peak CAPE exceeding 1,500–2,600 J/kg) favors scattered thunderstorm development across Kisumu and the surrounding basin between dusk and midnight (19:00 to 23:00 EAT). Temperatures will ease from current evening levels down to an overnight low of 20°C / 68°F under mostly cloudy skies. Light surface winds from the NW at 11 km/h (6 kt) may become locally gusty near any thunderstorm outflows. Ground air quality sensors have stale readings from earlier today (Ochieng' Avenue last reported 54 US AQI 3 hours ago); CAMS model data indicates US AQI levels around 89–90 (Moderate) tonight.

## Extended Outlook
For Tuesday through Thursday, expect warm daytime highs near 31°C / 88°F to 33°C / 91°F. Tuesday carries lingering evening rain chances, while Wednesday looks drier and settled. By Thursday (Day+3), numerical models converge on renewed shower activity across the basin, despite Kenya Met forecasting dry conditions. Looking further into the 4 to 7 day period, guidance shows a wetter pattern taking shape by next Monday (Day+7), led by ECMWF projecting up to 15.4 mm (0.61 in) of rainfall.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
High convective instability persists tonight, with model CAPE values reaching 1,340 to 5,000 J/kg (peaking around 19:00 EAT). Isolated thunderstorms remain possible through the evening and overnight hours, capable of brief downpours, frequent lightning, and sudden gusty winds.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Nocturnal thunderstorm hazards are elevated over open lake waters tonight as lake-breeze convergence combines with CAPE over 2,000 J/kg. Winds over the water will blow from the NW to N at 13 km/h (7 kt) with gusts up to 25 km/h (14 kt) outside of storm cell activity. Boaters and night fishermen should remain alert for sudden wind shifts and localized heavy rain through dawn.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1008 hPa) and highest toward the south (1019 hPa) — an 11 hPa spread, establishing a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is falling as deepening trends continue to the north and west. Across the Nyanza Basin, mean surface pressure sits around 1011 to 1015 hPa, maintaining a slight falling trend over 24–72 hours that supports low-level convergence and convective lifting.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
This update incorporates a fresher model cycle (last aligned at 06:00Z, 9 hours ago). Model disagreement on precipitation timing remains significant tonight—ECMWF, ICON, and Best Match bring rain and elevated CAPE into the evening, whereas GFS and UKMO keep precipitation totals negligible at the surface despite UKMO's extreme 5,000 J/kg CAPE call. On Day+0 rain calls, Best Match holds the top track record (81% all-time accuracy), while GFS remains weakest (63%) with a persistent wind speed overestimation bias (+21.0 km/h). Kenya Met forecasts light showers and thunderstorms over a few places for Tuesday with a high of 33.0°C / 91°F and low of 19.0°C / 66°F, offering a helpful local peer benchmark. Individual ground AQI stations (Kisumu Airport at 50 AQI, Ochieng' Avenue at 54 AQI, Dunga Beach at 41 AQI) are all stale by 3 hours, so CAMS model guidance is utilized for current atmospheric conditions.

earlier_issuances.narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Warm today with maximum temperatures feeling much like yesterday, before dry daytime conditions give way to evening showers. Thunderstorms are possible tonight peaking around 19:00 EAT as atmospheric instability develops, with models showing significant disagreement on shower timing; much the same through Thursday, with rain becoming more likely.

## Today's Forecast
Temperatures reaching a daytime high of 30°C / 86°F under sunny intervals through the morning and early afternoon. Peak solar UV exposure reaches a Very High index of 9.3 around midday. Ground air quality sensor readings are currently stale; the last reported reading was 74 AQI at Dunga Beach 3 hours ago, while CAMS model estimates indicate Moderate air quality (US AQI 85–92) across the city today. Surface winds will pick up from the SW at 18 km/h (10 kt) with gusts to 30 km/h (16 kt) during the afternoon. Rain probability increases late in the afternoon and into the evening (16:00 to 22:00 EAT) with potential isolated thunderstorms dropping around 2.5 mm (0.10 in) of rain locally. Temperatures will drop to an overnight low of 20°C / 68°F under partly to mostly cloudy skies.

## Extended Outlook
Over the next 3 days (Tuesday through Thursday), daytime maximum temperatures will remain steady around 30°C / 86°F to 32°C / 90°F. Rain chances gradually increase by Thursday as deeper moisture arrives across the Nyanza Basin. Looking ahead to the 4 to 7 day range (Friday through next Monday), guidance shows elevated uncertainty: ECMWF signals a much wetter trend by Day+7 with rainfall totals up to 15.4 mm (0.61 in), whereas GFS keeps conditions lighter and more isolated.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability is elevated across the basin today, with UKMO reaching a peak CAPE of 3,650 J/kg and ECMWF building to 1,420 J/kg around 19:00 EAT. Isolated thunderstorms capable of frequent lightning, sudden gusty winds, and brief heavy downpours are possible from late afternoon through dusk and overnight.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Morning winds across open lake waters will blow from the SE at 15 km/h (8 kt), veering to the SW/W at 20 km/h (11 kt) in the afternoon with gusts reaching 33 km/h (18 kt). High instability over the lake water (CAPE exceeding 1,500–2,000 J/kg on UKMO and ECMWF) supports nocturnal thunderstorm activity over open waters overnight. Boaters and fishermen should exercise caution after dusk.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1008 hPa) and highest toward the south (1019 hPa) — a 11 hPa spread, establishing a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is falling as a large-scale trough deepens to the north and west. Regionally across the Nyanza Basin, mean sea-level pressure ranges from 1014.4 hPa to 1016.6 hPa today and shows a gentle 24-to-72 hour falling trend, which favors enhanced convective development when combined with lake-breeze convergence.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
The model guidance behind this issuance is at least 9 hours old (models were last all aligned at 18:00Z). In model evaluations at Day+0, Best Match holds the highest rain verification record (81% all-time), while GFS is the weakest (63% all-time). GFS also exhibits a persistent, established bias of over-forecasting peak surface wind speeds (+21.0 km/h mean error), so its raw wind gust outputs have been discounted. For today's call, Kenya Met forecasts sunny intervals in the morning followed by light showers and thunderstorms in the afternoon/night with a high of 30.0°C / 86°F and low of 20.0°C / 68°F. This aligns closely with the blended call and ECMWF/ICON convective timing. Historical verification notes from similar high-CAPE setups (such as August 19 and 20) show that GFS often missed nocturnal lake convection while ECMWF and ICON correctly captured localized rainfall; thus, higher weight is given to ECMWF/ICON for late-day precipitation probabilities. Individual ground AQI stations reporting includes Kisumu Airport (A418534: 54 AQI, stale), Ochieng' Avenue (A418300: stale), and Dunga Beach (A418504: 74 AQI, stale).
